storyboards: Who inside can reach the sensitive bucket?

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 36. Title 'Who inside can reach the sensitive bucket?' Subtitle 'Internal access analysis reveals possible permission paths to a selected resource.' Main composition: a beautiful cutaway organization boundary spanning the page, with three account islands INSIDE it. Left two islands 'Account A · Analytics' and 'Account B · Engineering'; right large island 'Account C · Data'. Each account has recognizable role identity glyphs; the data island holds a richly colored green S3 bucket labeled 'Selected resource: finance-reports'. Draw TWO different curved cyan permission paths converging on the bucket: 'ReportReader' -> 'Direct resource access' -> bucket, and 'BuildRole' -> 'Assume DataReader' -> 'DataReader role' -> bucket. Label paths clearly 'Possible access paths — not observed traffic'. A magnifying glass (IAM Access Analyzer) sits OVER a segment of the paths and points with a dashed annotation line to an example finding 'Principal: BuildRole / Resource: finance-reports / Inspect how the role reaches the data'. Small number markers integrate into diagram: '1 Select supported sensitive resources', '2 Create an internal access analyzer', '3 Review principal and access path'. Along bottom, a small visual correction scene: orange policy document 'Narrow unintended trust or permission' -> rescan magnifier -> bucket with green shield 'Verify intended access still works'. Short caution 'Being inside the organization does not mean every access path is intended.' All internal actors must lie within organization boundary. No external attacker, no table, no claim access is actually observed or automatically removed. Resource selection and internal analyzer distinct from external analyzer.
Turn activity into a policy draft

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 37. Title 'Turn activity into a policy draft'. Subtitle 'CloudTrail history helps you start least privilege; review completes it.' NO TABLE. Main composition: an engaging editorial left-to-right transformation, with authentic miniature activity records flowing like paper receipts from a CloudTrail orange cloud/log glyph into a violet IAM Access Analyzer magnifier. At left a small EC2/workload role node labeled 'Select IAM role'. Above the trail feed a curved timeline band 'Choose a representative window · up to 90 days'. Show illustrative readable event labels 'DescribeInstances', 'DescribeVolumes', and 'Denied call' on three distinct receipts, under 'CloudTrail trail events'. Feed these receipts toward analyzer with a clearly named arrow 'Analyze activity'. Analyzer outputs one substantial amber-outlined document labeled 'Generated policy template' with short illustrative lines 'Review actions', 'Scope resources', 'Add conditions'. Then a large human review hand/pencil, not a generic icon square, traces edits on that document, labeled 'Review service-level gaps and required rare operations'. A lower curved branch demonstrates 'Review' -> 'Test normal and recovery workflows' -> 'Attach reviewed policy' with IAM role shield, no automatic attachment. Three compact note callouts orbit the template, not a table or equal cards: 'Data-event action detail is not generated'; 'iam:PassRole is not included'; 'Denied events are reviewed too'. Tiny no more than one footer sentence 'Observed activity is evidence for a draft, not proof of every permission the workload needs.' Keep every annotation legible. Do not show S3 GetObject as generated action-level output; do not claim all collected events are successful. Warm orange event receipts, violet analytical lens, cyan flow and green reviewed endpoint on DARK NAVY throughout.
Unused access needs a decision, not a delete button

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 38. Title 'Unused access needs a decision'. Subtitle 'A quiet permission may be unnecessary—or waiting for a recovery event.' NO TABLE. Main composition is a large dramatic annotated horizontal timeline occupying upper-middle, with three small daily-operation peaks, a long quiet period and a FUTURE disaster-recovery drill icon beyond a vertical 'Today' marker. A bracket spans past period labeled 'Configured tracking period'; no numeric duration needed. Show a small IAM role and fading permission key underneath quiet period with magnifier callout 'Unused-access finding: no recorded use in this window'. Label future drill 'Rare but required? Verify with the owner'. Crucial visual: lower-middle branching decision diamond 'Still required?' starting from 'Review role purpose + last accessed evidence'. Yes branch curves right to 'Keep narrowly scoped' -> 'Record reason and test recovery', with a protective lifebuoy/restore icon. No branch curves left to 'Remove unnecessary access' -> 'Test normal workloads', with scissors cutting an unused permission thread, not deleting a person or whole account. Avoid RED X on the Yes branch; both branches valid. A small outer curved cyan arrow returns both branches to 'Monitor and review again'. One clear footer 'Unused is a review signal; check workload and recovery requirements before changing access.' Attractive navy scene, purposeful gold clock/timeline, violet magnifier, teal path and glossy IAM identity icon. No table, no card grid, no promise automatic removal. Make it clear the observed quiet period is NOT evidence the recovery permission is never needed.
Simulate the request, then verify the workload

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 39. Title 'Simulate the request, then verify the workload'. Subtitle 'Test the action, resource and request context before a live validation.' NO TABLE. Create an attractive visual laboratory with one large left request capsule, a central branching evaluation path and a right real-workload boundary. Request capsule exact labels 'Illustrative custom policy test', 'Action: s3:GetObject', 'Resource: finance reports', 'Department tag: Finance'. From capsule arrow 'Simulation only' enters IAM Policy Simulator violet magnifier/shield with small tag 'Custom mode: supplied policies'. Below lens one compact decision diamond 'Action + resource + condition match?' branching green 'Yes' to 'ALLOW in simulation', and orange 'No matching allow' to 'IMPLICIT DENY in simulation'. Both outcomes connect with thin neutral line to a smaller explanatory document 'Inspect policy and supplied context'; no automatic link deny->production. At far right distinct bright green-bordered sandbox labeled 'Controlled live test', containing actual workload role -> S3 bucket with object-return arrow, and a check 'Verify expected read and a denied case'. Draw one clearly labeled dashed connector from simulation review to live test 'After review, validate in AWS'. Crucial short label near simulator 'No AWS service request is made'. Under the live boundary label 'Other applicable controls and runtime conditions still matter'. One meaningful caution 'Simulation results can differ from the live environment.' Make simulation vs live visually distinct. No fabricated console screenshot, no table, no false blanket claims about unsupported policies. Give central policy logic room, modest dimensional icons, gold/cyan/purple accents on full dark navy, white large teaching text.
